situation: A JSON serializer for an API response traverses a graph of entities to build a payload. Some entities reference each other (e.g., author -> posts -> author). The serializer enters infinite recursion and the request times out.
deadEnds: Set a maximum recursion depth, which prevented the crash but silently truncated valid deeply-nested data
Tried converting the graph to a tree by removing back-references before serialization, but this mutated the original data and broke downstream consumers
Used JSON.stringify, which also fails on circular references and throws a TypeError
unlock: Tracking already-visited objects in a Set (or WeakSet) allowed the serializer to detect cycles and replace back-references with a sentinel (like { $ref: '#/path' }) instead of recursing infinitely. The same pattern applies to any recursive traversal over potentially cyclic structures.
